summary: Facepalm: I'm submitting two new facepalm candidates, both institutional election errors in the Oct. 18–24 window and both opened and checked word for word. The first is the Utah County clerk's office sending ID-required notices to voters who didn't need them (KSL.com and the Salt Lake Tribune). The second is Bexar County, Texas, early-voting ballots that showed another school district's measure in place of East Central ISD's Prop A (KSAT and TPR). The Bexar story was set aside on Oct. 23 only because its headline was too long; it is resubmitted with a shorter one. Neither subject is a politician acting as one, so party is null. I passed on Westmoreland County, Pa. (only one independent accepted source) and a few others. My search budget ran out before I could find a third or fourth candidate. Genius: Genius scan for 2026-10-24 (window Oct 18–24). No candidate met the rules. The search budget ran out partway through the scan. The best lead was the Northwestern single-positron trap (Physical Review Letters, about Oct 21), which is in the US and inside the window. But again, none of the accepted pages would open: Phys.org returned 'not accessible', Scientific American was blocked, and Northwestern's release (both versions) returned 'not allowed'. Two other in-window US leads had only one accepted page that opened (Science News): Yale's levitated nanoparticle detecting single gas-atom collisions (PRL, Oct 23) and Quantinuum's error-correction result (an arXiv preprint posted Oct 19). I also went through the ScienceDaily reposts from Oct 19–23. All of them turned out to be too old, not US-based, or associations rather than achievements. No genius story met the standard; nothing published. The verified facepalm story is on the bench for a later day.

candidates.headline: Utah County clerk's office wrongly tells some voters their mail ballots need a copy of their ID
candidates.reason: passed every check; kept for a later day because the other side had no story

candidates.headline: Bexar County, Texas, early ballots show another district's measure instead of East Central ISD's Prop A
Westmoreland County, Pa., sends 157 duplicate mail ballots to voters
candidates.reason: In the window (reported Oct. 23), but only one independent accepted source. The Votebeat article was co-reported with Spotlight PA (not accepted). The abc27 page is a Spotlight PA republication, and it returned 'url_not_accessible'. WESA's copy is on wesanews.org, which isn't on the accepted list.

candidates.headline: Summit County, Utah, reissues about 50 ballots that left off the Basin Recreation bond question
candidates.reason: In the window (Oct. 21–22), but the only coverage found was KPCW, TownLift and The Park Record, none of which is on the accepted list.

candidates.headline: West Orange, N.J., mayoral candidate's home tracked by AirTag on missing anti-candidate signs
candidates.reason: The alleged sign theft would have a victim (the sign owner), and the candidate's campaign disputes it, so no blunder is established. Only one accepted source (ABC7 NY) was found.

candidates.headline: Dozens of undelivered ballots found in a dumpster near a Seattle park
candidates.reason: It isn't clear who was responsible, and it may involve mail theft with victims. No responsible institution's blunder is established.

candidates.headline: Northwestern physicists trap a single positron for months in a 'one-positron quantum cyclotron' (Physical Review Letters)
candidates.reason: In the US and inside the window, but none of the accepted pages could be opened. Phys.org returned 'not accessible', Scientific American returned 'url not allowed', and Northwestern's release (both the main and journalist versions) was not allowed. The rest of the coverage (sci.news, Tech Times, technology.org, Yahoo, Eurasia Review, Slashdot) is not accepted.

candidates.headline: Yale team's levitated nanoparticle detects the impact of single gas atoms (Physical Review Letters, Oct. 23)
candidates.reason: Only one accepted source opened (Science News, Oct. 22). The APS journal and Physics Magazine pages were not accessible, and Physics World is not accepted. Science magazine's own story is about 44 days old: it covered the preprint and predates the journal publication.

candidates.headline: Quantinuum's Helios logical qubit makes about 5 errors per million operations (Broomfield, Colo.)
candidates.reason: The result is an arXiv preprint posted Oct. 19 and has not been peer-reviewed. The only accepted source is Science News, and the rest of the coverage (The Quantum Insider, Quantum Computing Report, PostQuantum) is not accepted.

candidates.headline: Van Gogh's 'The Starry Night' matched to the pre-dawn sky of July 22, 1889 (Scientific Reports, Oct. 22)
candidates.reason: Not in the US. The study was led by Elijah Jeong-hyun Kim of SLLAB and Kyung Hee University in South Korea. The findings are also hedged ('may have been based').

candidates.headline: MIT engineers build a paper-thin swimming robot powered by light-controlled muscle cells
candidates.reason: Too old. ScienceDaily's Oct. 23 page republishes an MIT News story dated Sept. 29, 2026.

candidates.headline: Allen Institute maps targeted signalling by locus coeruleus noradrenaline neurons (Nature)
candidates.reason: Too old. The Nature paper was published Sept. 16, 2026, and ScienceDaily's Oct. 23 page is a repost. It is also a mouse study.

candidates.headline: Ole Bielfeldt wins first place in the 2026 Nikon Small World photomicrography competition (Oct. 21)
candidates.reason: Not in the US. According to Science News, the winner is a design student in Cologne, Germany.

candidates.headline: Texas A&M: FDA-cleared personalized brain-stimulation PTSD treatment reports 68% remission
candidates.reason: The only source is a ScienceDaily repost of a university release, and the date of the FDA clearance was not confirmed inside the window. It is closer to a product clearance than a distinct achievement.

candidates.headline: Case Western study finds swapping gas stoves for electric ones eased asthma symptoms in Cleveland homes
candidates.reason: A before-and-after health study rather than a distinct achievement. The journal DOI (jaip.2026.06.039) suggests it was published before the window, and the only accepted source is Science News.

candidates.headline: UChicago first-principles calculations of internal conversion in spin defects (Physical Review Letters)
candidates.reason: A theoretical calculation with no demonstrated result. The only accepted source is a ScienceDaily repost.
